payload.title: Wedding Timeline for a 4pm Ceremony With 2pm to 5pm Options
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: A couple in their 30s, about a year out from a destination or multi-event wedding, who has a venue or region in mind and now needs to set the ceremony time and see how the rest of the day (and the guests' travel) falls around it, before they brief their venue and photographer.
payload.goal: Start a conversation with a Wedded Advisor through the Wedded Concierge enquiry form to have the day's timing worked out with the venue.
secondary_links: /expert-advice/wedding-day-timeline (head page, link prominently near the top; it should link back here)
/wonderland-studio (described only as 'our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs')
payload.angle: An original hour-by-hour wedding day built around a 4pm ceremony, then 2pm, 3pm and 5pm versions that show exactly what moves when the ceremony time moves: the light, the heat, the gap before dinner, and how guests get there. Framed for destination and multi-event weddings, where curfews, local timing customs, same-day guest arrivals and guests watching from other time zones change the maths. Every clock time is an example to adapt ('for example'), never a rule or a statistic, and sunset is something the reader checks for their own venue and date from an official source.
must_include: Direct-answer intro (what a 4pm ceremony day looks like in a sentence or two), followed by exactly 4 one-sentence takeaways.

The 4pm example timeline, in order: getting ready, first look or photos, guest arrival, ceremony, drinks and photos, reception entrance, dinner, speeches, first dance, the send-off. Times framed as 'for example'.
2pm, 3pm and 5pm example timelines, each with a short note on what changes versus 4pm (light, heat, the gap before dinner, guest travel).
Light and season section: tell readers to check the official sunset time for their venue and date, link an official source at the claim, and state no sunset times.
Destination factors written as questions to ask the venue: curfews and noise rules, local timing customs, guests arriving the same day, and time zones for guests watching remotely.
A copyable timeline template table (blank or example times the reader can adapt).

Close with one Wedded Advisor line drawn only from brand-facts 'Claims we can make' (for example: one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, working in your time zone), linking /wonderland-concierge with UTM.
Prominent link to /expert-advice/wedding-day-timeline near the top as the full-day guide.
avoid: The phrase 'last dance' anywhere (including the brand-facts Advisor definition wording); use 'the send-off' or 'the end of the night'.
Prices of any kind, 'From AUD' figures, statistics, 'best', 'free', vendor names.
Stated sunset times or any clock time presented as a rule, average or statistic.
Research or process talk ('our research shows', 'top results', 'SERP').
Advisor claims outside 'Claims we can make': no transfers, 'on the ground', room blocks, availability, phone line or a named person.
Describing Wonderland Studio as anything other than 'our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs'.
Competitor names, wording or formats copied from ranking pages.
Clichés (fairytale, dream day), em dashes, US spelling.
Re-covering ceremony length, ceremony order or scripts in depth; summarise and link the owning pages.
Linking drafts; link only pages confirmed live.
payload.cannibalisation_check: /expert-advice/wedding-day-timeline is the head for the general wedding day timeline (no primary keyword recorded in the link map) and may currently hold the GSC impressions for 'wedding day timeline 2pm ceremony'. This post differs by owning ceremony-time-specific schedules (4pm, plus 2pm, 3pm and 5pm variants) and the destination timing factors; the head should link here with ceremony-time anchor text and keep its general overview. Adjacent, no keyword clash: /expert-advice/how-long-is-a-wedding-ceremony (ceremony length), /expert-advice/what-happens-in-a-wedding-ceremony (ceremony order), /expert-advice/wedding-ceremony-script (scripts), /expert-advice/wedding-planning-checklist and /meh-to-magnificent-wedding-planning-timeline (months-out planning, not the day itself). Possible partial overlap to watch: /your-pre-ceremony-wedding-schedule-sorted (pre-ceremony schedule) and /the-ultimate-wedding-planning-checklist-and-timeline; neither targets a ceremony-time keyword, so link where useful rather than compete.
